Subject: Mosaic renewal — flexible term + overflow credit proposal

Laura —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Based on our conversation and your Q2 usage profile, attached is a proposal that aims to:

- Preserve the 6% unit discount you valued across committed usage,
- Add a 3-month price-hold for any committed SKU while we onboard your billing cadence, and
- Offer an overflow credit bucket (applies to burst usage above commit) that converts at a reduced fee rather than at pay-go rates.

Key trade-offs we discussed: a 12-month committed baseline vs a 24-month step-down where the effective price is held for the first 12 months and then reduced commit steps thereafter. The term sheet spells out both options — page 2 has a short comparison table.

Next steps I propose:
1) You review the attached term sheet and Q2 usage doc.
2) If numbers look plausible, I can kick off legal for a short form amendment and send a DocuSign for signature.
3) We’ll schedule a 30-minute ops sync with David to confirm burst routing and KV cache expectations.

I’ve cc’d Ben and David for pricing and onboarding context.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: Mosaic follow-up + recommended concessions

Team —

Summary of Laura's asks: 12m preferred term, overflow-credit semantics, net45 invoice term. They want firm commercial language for legal.

My recommended offer to get this signed this quarter (we're at risk of slipping into next fiscal):
- Commit: 12-month firm baseline at current proposed committed units, retaining the 6% unit discount.
- Price-hold: Guarantee the quoted unit price for the first 12 months (no step-down needed).
- Overflow credits: Provide a pooled monthly overflow credit equal to 40% of the customer's average monthly overage from Q2; unused credits expire after 2 months (no carryforward past that). Credits apply automatically as an invoice-line deduction; any overage beyond the bucket will be charged at the reduced overflow rate (not pay-go).
- Invoice terms: Approve net45 for first year; require ACH setup and standard overdue interest thereafter.

Trade-offs to note: the pooled credit with short expiry protects Redwood against long-term carry liabilities while giving Mosaic predictability. If leadership wants a longer carryforward window we should ask for a slightly higher commit or a reduced discount.

Can Marissa confirm legal ok on the short expiry language and finance confirm net45 internal signoff? If approved, Camila — I can prepare the final term sheet and the DocuSign envelope today.

Thanks —
Ben
Head of Renewal Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Final: Mosaic 12m renewal with overflow-credit bucket + net45 (DocuSign ready)

Laura / Procurement —

Appreciate the quick replies and clarity on constraints. Based on internal alignment with Ben/Marissa/David we can confirm the following commercial terms for a 12-month renewal:

- Commit: 12 months, committed baseline equal to projected Q3 runrate, with 6% unit discount applied to committed units.
- Price-hold: Quoted unit price will be held for the full 12-month term.
- Overflow credits: Monthly pooled credit equal to 40% of average monthly overage from Q2. Unused credits expire after 2 months. Credits apply as invoice deductions. Overages beyond the credit will be charged at the agreed overflow rate (lower than pay-go).
- Invoice terms: Net45 for the first 12 months. We’ll include ACH instructions on the first invoice; standard overdue interest applies after due date.

I have attached the final term sheet and usage summary. If this looks good to you, the DocuSign envelope is live here: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?s=renewal-mosaic-9073 (DocuSign: Renewal_Contract_Mosaic_9073).

Attachments: [Mosaic_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf (pdf), mosaic_q2_usage_summary.csv (csv)]
